classification.difficultyReason: Choose a common area and construct three figures satisfying it while deliberately varying and checking their perimeters; dimensions and construction choices are unsupplied.

content.prompt: Draw three figures, based on rectangles and triangles, that have the same area but different perimeters.

answer.short:
Sample answers: a $3\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ rectangle, a $6\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ rectangle and a right triangle with perpendicular sides $3\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$ and hypotenuse $5\text{ cm}$.

Each has area $6\text{ cm}^2$; their perimeters are $10\text{ cm}$, $14\text{ cm}$ and $12\text{ cm}$, respectively.
answer.worked:
Sample answers are shown in the figures.

For the $3\text{ cm}\times2\text{ cm}$ rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}A_1&=3\times2\\A_1&=6\text{ cm}^2\\P_1&=3+2+3+2\\P_1&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
For the $6\text{ cm}\times1\text{ cm}$ rectangle:
$$\begin{align*}A_2&=6\times1\\A_2&=6\text{ cm}^2\\P_2&=6+1+6+1\\P_2&=14\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
For the right triangle:
$$\begin{align*}A_3&=\frac12\times3\times4\\A_3&=6\text{ cm}^2\\P_3&=3+4+5\\P_3&=12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
All three areas are equal, while the three perimeters are different.
